title: One-dimensional components and strict henselization
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], put $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $\bar x$ be a geometric point over its closed point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Then $T$ has an irreducible component of dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] if and only if its strict localization $T_{(\bar x)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] has an irreducible component of dimension one.

source.place: Expose XIV, Lemma 2.1.5 (flatness and integrality of the strict-henselization map)

proof.text: Write $B=A^{\mathrm{sh}}_{T,\bar x}$ and $f:A\to B$ for the structural map. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples], the pointed-neighbourhood colimit defining $B$ is canonically, as an $A$-algebra, the triples colimit for the prime $\mathfrak m_A$ and the separable closure of $\kappa(\mathfrak m_A)$ inside the field of $\bar x$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples]: $B$ is henselian local, is a filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras, and $f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$. Thus it is ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Moreover [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] makes $f$ faithfully flat, hence flat by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Expose XIV, Lemma 2.1.5, proof (printed p. 210): flatness, integrality and surjectivity of the strict-localization map.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-ind-etale-local-henselian-integral] to $f$. Its prime is $\mathfrak m_A$, so $B$ is integral over the henselization $H$ of $A_{\mathfrak m_A}$. Here $A_{\mathfrak m_A}\cong A$: a fraction $a/s$ maps to $as^{-1}$ since $s\notin\mathfrak m_A$ is a unit. Since $A$ is henselian, the structural map $\eta:A\to H$ is an isomorphism by [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Explicitly the universal property gives $r:H\to A$ with $r\eta=1_A$; uniqueness applied to the maps $H\to H$ over $A$ gives $\eta r=1_H$. Replace every coefficient of a monic equation over $H$ by its inverse image under $\eta$; compatibility of the structural maps gives a monic equation over $A$. Hence $f$ is integral. Also $f$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] with $N=A$, under $A\otimes_A B\cong B$, $a\otimes b\mapsto f(a)b$.

source.place: Expose XIV, Lemma 2.1.5, proof (printed p. 210): flatness, integrality and surjectivity of the strict-localization map.

proof.text: If $\mathfrak q$ is a minimal prime of $B$, then $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ is minimal in $A$. Indeed, if $\mathfrak p'\subseteq\mathfrak p$ is prime, flat going down [lem-sc-flat-going-down] supplies a prime $\mathfrak q'\subseteq\mathfrak q$ contracting to $\mathfrak p'$. Minimality forces $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak q$, hence $\mathfrak p'=\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Expose XIV, Lemma 2.1.5, proof (printed p. 210): flatness, integrality and surjectivity of the strict-localization map.

proof.text: Conversely let $\mathfrak p$ be a minimal prime of $A$. The integral injective map $f$ has a prime $\mathfrak Q$ over $\mathfrak p$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over]. Choose a minimal prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak Q$ of $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] with $I=0$. Its contraction is a prime contained in $\mathfrak p$ and therefore equals $\mathfrak p$. Thus every minimal prime downstairs has a minimal prime above it. No bijection of minimal primes is asserted or needed.

source.place: Expose XIV, Lemma 2.1.5, proof (printed p. 210): flatness, integrality and surjectivity of the strict-localization map.

proof.text: For a minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ and $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, the induced homomorphism $\bar f:A/\mathfrak p\to B/\mathfrak q$ is injective: $f(a)\in\mathfrak q$ is equivalent to $a\in\mathfrak p$. It is integral: for $b+\mathfrak q$, take a monic equation for $b$ over $A$ from Step 2 and reduce every coefficient modulo $\mathfrak p$ and the equation modulo $\mathfrak q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal] to obtain $\dim(A/\mathfrak p)=\dim(B/\mathfrak q)$.

source.place: Expose XIV, Lemma 2.1.5, proof (printed p. 210): flatness, integrality and surjectivity of the strict-localization map.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], the components of $T$ and $T_{(\bar x)}=\operatorname{Spec}B$ are respectively $V_A(\mathfrak p)$ and $V_B(\mathfrak q)$ for minimal primes. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus] these subspaces are homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak q)$. Their topological dimensions are the corresponding ring dimensions by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; homeomorphisms preserve chains of irreducible closed subsets and their lengths. Step 3 associates to every component upstairs a minimal prime downstairs, and Step 5 preserves its dimension. Step 4 lifts every minimal prime downstairs to one upstairs, and Step 5 again preserves the dimension. Applying these two implications to dimension one proves the equivalence.

source.place: Expose XIV, Lemma 2.1.5, proof (printed p. 210): flatness, integrality and surjectivity of the strict-localization map.
